base.description: Roles and permissions are global to the deployment. The default.

workspaces.description: Users belong to workspaces and hold different roles in each. Workspace-scoped requests carry an X-Workspace-Id header.

postInstall: Set DATABASE_URL and AUTH_JWT_SECRET in .env (see .env.example). AUTH_JWT_SECRET must be base64, 256-bit or longer: openssl rand -base64 32 — there is no default and the app refuses to start without it.

Heads up: the root config files this installed (package.json, tsconfig*.json, oxlint/prettier/commitlint, docker-compose.yml, nest-cli.json) were overwritten, not merged — review the diff before committing.
Run: npm install, then npx prisma generate && npx prisma migrate deploy
Run: npm run seed — idempotent, seeds the permission catalog and the default admin/member roles. Nothing is authorized until it has run at least once.
Optional: set SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL and SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD before seeding to also create an initial admin user.

Write your own main.ts and app.module.ts — this ships the auth layer, not the application shell. app.module.ts needs: ConfigModule.forRoot(), ThrottlerModule.forRoot([...]), CoreAuthModule.forRoot({}), the 5 feature modules (Auth, Admin, Role, Permission, AuditLog), and APP_GUARD ThrottlerGuard + APP_FILTER AuthCoreErrorFilter + APP_INTERCEPTOR ResponseInterceptor.
In main.ts: app.setGlobalPrefix("api", { exclude: ["/", "health"] }) — routes are already versioned under v1, so they serve at /api/v1/auth/..., /api/v1/admin/..., etc.
Optional: setupDocs(app) in main.ts serves Swagger at /docs and Scalar at /reference.

Optional: setupMetrics(app) in main.ts serves Prometheus metrics at GET /metrics (request rate, latency, 401/403s, Node runtime). Set METRICS_TOKEN to require a bearer token on every scrape. A Grafana + Prometheus + node_exporter stack is installed at monitoring/ — see monitoring/README.md.

Logging: line-delimited JSON under ./logs/<date>/ (LOG_DIR overrides). Register APP_INTERCEPTOR RequestLoggerInterceptor *before* ResponseInterceptor to enable it. Rotation/retention is yours to arrange.
Then: npm run start:dev
Full docs (setup, API reference, RBAC, dev loop): https://github.com/shahriar-ratul/simple-auth-kit/tree/main/docs

workspaces: Workspace-scoped requests must send an X-Workspace-Id header — see WorkspaceController and authz.guard.ts
A user has no roles until they belong to a workspace: POST /workspaces makes the caller its first admin
Roles are scoped to a workspace here, so the seeder also creates the first one — set SEED_WORKSPACE_NAME to name it (defaults to "Default workspace")

postInstall: Copy .env.example to .env and set VITE_AUTH_API_URL to your running simple-auth-kit backend's URL
Run: npm install (or pnpm install) in the generated directory

If this isn't already a git repository, run: git init — husky's pre-commit/commit-msg hooks (wired via the "prepare": "husky" script) only activate once a .git directory exists; without one, npm install's prepare step no-ops harmlessly
Run: npm run dev — starts the Vite dev server

workspaces: Pair with a workspaces-variant backend (e.g. nestjs-prisma --workspaces) — this console sends X-Workspace-Id on every workspace-scoped request

postInstall: Run: npm install (or pnpm install) in the generated directory

If this isn't already a git repository, run: git init — husky's pre-commit/commit-msg hooks (wired via the "prepare": "husky" script) only activate once a .git directory exists; without one, npm install's prepare step no-ops harmlessly

Run: npm start — opens the Expo dev tools (android/ios/web from there)

iOS only: run pod install inside ios/ before the first build
Set the backend URL your platform actually needs — see src/api/authClient.ts (Android emulator: 10.0.2.2, not localhost)

postInstall: Copy .env.example to .env and set NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_API_URL to your running simple-auth-kit backend's URL
Run: npm install (or pnpm install) in the generated directory

If this isn't already a git repository, run: git init — husky's pre-commit/commit-msg hooks (wired via the "prepare": "husky" script) only activate once a .git directory exists; without one, npm install's prepare step no-ops harmlessly
Run: npm run dev — starts the Next.js dev server on port 3000

Note: base and workspaces variants deliberately use different route-guarding trust models — base uses NextAuth edge middleware (src/proxy.ts), workspaces uses a client-side session recheck on every navigation. Both are correct for their own architecture; see registry/admin-apps/README.md for why they aren't unified.

base: Also set AUTH_SECRET in .env — the NextAuth v5 session-JWT signing secret. Generate one with: npx auth secret (or: openssl rand -base64 32)
workspaces: Pair with a workspaces-variant backend (e.g. nestjs-prisma --workspaces) — this console sends X-Workspace-Id on every workspace-scoped request
